**Subject:** The Quiet Frequency is out today

Hi there,

*The Quiet Frequency* is out today.

> A dying alien mind. A burned-out spy. One last signal.

Retired spy Slade Quintz has spent years hiding at Cape Sorrow, a dead weather station on the Oregon coast, with his loyal Malinois, Cipher, and a duct-taped android named Sebastion. Then every machine he owns starts pulsing to the same rhythm.

It's a voice: a dying colony of living light high above Earth, blacking out the grid every time it cries for help.

To answer it, Slade needs the woman he abandoned nine years ago. A storm is coming, and powerful people want the colony as a weapon.

Here's a taste of Slade's mornings:

*"The first thing I do every morning is check whether the world has ended. The world has not ended. It has only gotten stranger, a distinction I used to get paid to make."*

If you like wry, character-driven first-contact stories (think *Project Hail Mary*) and weary-spy thrillers (think *Slow Horses*), this one is for you. It's about listening and being heard, second chances, found family, and the courage to stay. One week of fog, storm, and an alien voice, with a deadpan robot butler along for the ride.

Subject: A dying alien voice, a burned-out spy, and a duct-taped android

Hi there,

The first thing Slade Quintz does every morning is check whether the world has ended.

*"The world has not ended. It has only gotten stranger, a distinction I used to get paid to make."*

That's the opening of **The Quiet Frequency**, my science fiction thriller. Slade is a retired spy hiding at Cape Sorrow, a dead weather station on the Oregon coast, with his bad-hipped Malinois, Cipher, and Sebastion, a deadpan android held together with duct tape. Then every machine he owns starts pulsing to the same rhythm.

It's a voice, a dying colony of living light high above Earth, blacking out the grid each time it cries for help. To answer it, Slade needs the woman he abandoned nine years ago. A storm is coming, and powerful people want the colony as a weapon.
